sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned Counsel for the parties.
3. Complainant - Smt. Smita is the wife of the petitioner herein.

On 13.09.2022, she had filed a complaint before the Puttenahalli Police Station, Bengaluru City, against the petitioner herein alleging that he had sexually assaulted her NC: 2023:KHC:33542 minor daughter aged about 12 years.

Initially FIR was registered in Crime No.227/2022 by Puttenahalli police against the petitioner on the basis of the said complaint for the offences punishable under Sections 4, 5(l), 5(m),
6 & 7 of the POCSO Act.
Subsequently, for want of jurisdiction, the said complaint was transferred and registered before the Tumakuru Women Police Station in Crime No.121/2022.

sentences.text: In the complaint, it is averred that the complainant was married to the petitioner in the year 2008 and the couple have a girl child aged about 12 years.
On 09.09.2022, when the biology teacher of the minor girl was teaching her about bad touch and good touch in her school, the minor girl allegedly started weeping.

When the teacher inquired her, she informed that about three years earlier, when she was studying in 5th Standard i.e., in the month of December in the year 2019, petitioner herein in the guise of showing her games in his mobile phone, had sexually assaulted her.
The complainant was, therefore, summoned to the school by the teacher and informed about the alleged sexual assault that was revealed by the minor girl.

On inquiry by the complainant, she was informed by the minor girl that about three years prior to the NC: 2023:KHC:33542 date of complaint, in their earlier house at Gandhinagar in Tumakuru, when the petitioner and the minor girl were at home, on the guise of showing games in the mobile phone of the petitioner, he had committed sexual assault on the minor girl and this act was repeated by him number of times thereafter.
The petitioner allegedly had threatened the minor girl, and therefore, she had not revealed the same to anybody.

It is in this background, complainant had approached the police on 13.09.2022 and lodged a complaint, which had ultimately resulted in registering FIR in Crime No.121/2022 by Tumakuru Women Police Station.
5. During the course of investigation, petitioner was arrested on 15.09.2022.
His bail application filed by the Addl. District & Sessions Judge, FTC-1, Tumakuru, in Crl. Misc.No.1899/2022 was dismissed on 26.12.2022.

entities.text: Addl. District & Sessions Judge, FTC-1, Tumakuru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is under these circumstances, petitioner is before this Court.

6. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that there is a serious matrimonial dispute between the complainant and the petitioner and as a result, the petitioner has been falsely implicated in a criminal case.
He submits that NC: 2023:KHC:33542 the material on record would go to show that the parties have been litigating in number of cases before the Court and they have separated in the year 2010 itself.
He also submits that the petitioner is a resident of Davanagere and the complainant and her daughter are residing at Tumakuru.
Petitioner is in custody since 15.09.2022.
Investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed, and
accordingly prays to allow the petition.
7. Per contra, learned HCGP and the learned Counsel for the defacto complainant have strongly opposed the petition.
They submit that petitioner who is the father of the minor girl has indulged in committing sexual assault against his minor daughter.
The minor daughter has mentioned about the act committed by the petitioner in detail during the course of her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.PC.
Under the circumstances, they pray to dismiss the petition.

8. As per the complaint averments, petitioner allegedly had committed sexual assault on his minor daughter in the month of December 2019 when the minor daughter was studying in 5th Standard at Tumakuru.

For the first time, the said incident NC: 2023:KHC:33542 was allegedly revealed by the minor girl in her school to her teacher when she was being thought about good touch and bad touch by her teacher on 09.09.2022.
9.
The material on record would go to show that the marriage of the petitioner and the complainant was performed in the year 2008 and the girl child was born to them in the year 2009.

In the year Joseph Luke.S vs State Of Karnataka on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84277676/
3 2010, complainant had left the company of the petitioner along with the child and had started to reside at Tumakuru.

sentences.text: Petitioner had, therefore, got issued a legal notice on 14.07.2010 to the complainant for restitution of conjugal rights.

After service of notice, since the complainant had not responded to the same, petitioner had filed M.C.No.179/2010 before the Family Court at Davanagere where he was residing, with a prayer to grant a decree of restitution of conjugal rights.
In the said proceedings, the address of the complainant is shown at Tumakuru.

The said petition was decreed by the Family Court, Davanagere, on 22.03.2011 and a decree was passed against the complainant directing the complainant to join the company of the petitioner and to discharge her marital obligations and duties.
It appears that the complainant had not complied with the said decree.
Therefore, the petitioner had NC: 2023:KHC:33542 filed Execution Case No.4/2015 before the Family Court at Davanagere.

10. In the meanwhile, complainant and her minor daughter had filed C.Misc. No.96/2014 before the Family Court at Tumakuru, under Section 125 of Cr.PC with a prayer to grant maintenance of Rs.6,000/- & Rs.4,000/- per month, respectively, to them.
In the said petition, it is averred that the petitioner was ill-treating and assaulting the complainant and was treating her in a bad manner.
It was also stated that he was not maintaining the complainant and her minor daughter and the complainant who was unemployed, was finding it difficult to maintain herself and her minor daughter.
In the said petition which was filed in the year 2014, complainant's address is shown at Tumakuru, whereas the address of the petitioner is shown at Davanagere.
Petitioner had filed a detailed objection statement to the said petition on 23.09.2015,

In the said statement of objections,
petitioner has stated that the complainant has not complied with the decree of restitution of conjugal rights, and therefore, Execution Case No.4/2015 was filed before the Family Court at Davanagere which was pending consideration.

All the aforesaid aspects of the matter have been suppressed by the complainant, and on the other hand, she has filed a complaint which prima facie reflects as if the petitioner and the complainant were living together.
There is nothing on record to show that the complainant had honoured the decree of restitution of conjugal rights and had started living with the petitioner.

All the records made available to the Court would go to show that the petitioner is residing in Davanagere, whereas in the complaint it is alleged that the petitioner and the complainant were residing at Tumakuru, but there is no material to establish the same.

12. As per the charge sheet allegations, the house at Tumakuru in which the complainant was living,
was taken on rent by her.

Having regard to the fact that the relationship between the petitioner and the complainant was strained since the year 2010 itself and also considering the fact that they have been litigating in various courts thereafter, wherein the address of the petitioner is shown at Davanagere and the address of the complainant is shown at Tumakuru, it becomes NC:
2023:KHC:33542 highly doubtful that the petitioner and the complainant were staying together in Tumakuru during the year 2019.

sentences.text: Investigation in the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed.
Petitioner is in custody since 15.09.2022.

Under the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case and considering the conduct of the complainant who has suppressed the material fact before the police regarding her strained relationship with the petitioner from the year 2010 onwards, I am of the considered view that the prayer made by the petitioner for grant of regular bail requires to be answered affirmatively.

Accordingly, the following order:
14.
The petition is allowed.
